overlap.title: Overlap degrades both lexical recognition and speaker attribution.
overlap.description: Within-inference-unit comparison between non-overlapped utterances and utterances with at least 50% overlap exposure.
overlap.note: All reported overlap penalties are statistically significant.

similarity.title: Acoustic speaker similarity is a consistent source of attribution error.
similarity.description: Spearman correlation between pairwise speaker similarity and pairwise confusion on completely non-overlapping utterances.
similarity.note: All seven correlations are positive and significant (p < 0.05).

acoustic.title: Acoustic degradation primarily affects lexical recognition.
acoustic.description: Correlation between the recording-level acoustic degradation score d_N and error measures on utterances without overlap and away from speaker-turn boundaries.
acoustic.note: Correlations with E_lex are significant for all systems; correlations with E_attr are weak and significant for only one system.

turn.title: Speaker transitions primarily disrupt who spoke, rather than what was said.
turn.description: Within-inference-unit attribution penalty near non-overlapping speaker switches using a ±0.5 s boundary neighborhood.
turn.note: The E_attr penalty is significant for every evaluated system; neither E_lex nor E_seg is significant for any system.

speaker.title: Higher speaker count is associated with greater speaker-attribution difficulty.
speaker.description: Speaker-number association after controlling for dataset identity and overlap ratio; P3 is excluded to reduce dataset-specific bias.
speaker.note: Controlled analysis—not a raw P0→P3 trend. SoulX-Transcriber is excluded because its 5-minute units do not always contain every recording-level speaker.
